title: Airy High-Hydration Ciabatta
description: Soft, open-crumb Italian bread using a liquid-dough method. Big holes, crisp crust, zero nonsense.

method.instruction: In a large bowl, mix 250 ml of warm water, sugar, and yeast. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Add 40 ml of olive oil and 400 g of the bread flour. Mix until smooth.
Add the remaining 252 ml of water and the remaining 600 g of bread flour. Add salt. Mix to a very wet, sticky dough.
With wet hands, stretch and fold the dough several times. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Repeat stretch and fold. Cover and rest for another 20 minutes.
Oil hands with the remaining 15 ml of olive oil and fold once more. Cover and let rise for 1 hour until bubbly and doubled in size.
Heavily flour the work surface with the remaining 30 g of bread flour. Turn out dough and dust lightly. Do not punch down.
Gently stretch into a rectangle — no kneading. Fold once, then cut into 6 pieces.
Transfer to a heavily floured baking tray. Rest for 20 minutes.
Bake for 15–25 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing to preserve the open crumb.

notes.title: Wet Hands
notes.content: This dough is extremely sticky — keep your hands wet when handling it, not floured. Water prevents sticking without adding extra flour that would weigh down the dough.

notes.title: No Deflating
notes.content: Do not punch down the dough when shaping. The large air bubbles are what give ciabatta its characteristic open crumb. Handle it gently and only fold, never knead.
